answers.answer: Each player chooses a color and places that color's Player ID card visibly in front of them. They receive the Voting card set with that color on its backs; cards targeting colors not in play are removed, while the player's own Ambush is kept. Deal four Gold Bar cards face down to the center with values hidden.
answers.evidence: Setup: choose a color and stand its Player ID visibly; remove cards targeting colors that are not playing; keep your own Ambush; deal four Gold Bar cards face down to the center.

answers.answer: There is no individual player-by-player turn order. A player may change their chosen card until cards are revealed. Once everyone has chosen, all choices are revealed simultaneously.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure: “There is no individual turn order.” Vote: “You may change your chosen card until cards are revealed” and then “reveal all choices simultaneously.”

answers.answer: No. Red is a Target with three votes because the player receiving the most votes is the Target; no majority or four-vote threshold is stated. Blue and Green, tied below Red, are not Targets.
answers.evidence: Vote: “The player receiving the most votes is the Target. If several players tie for the most votes, all of them are Targets.”

answers.answer: Both Red and Blue are Targets because they tie for the most votes. With neither protected by a successful Ambush, both are eliminated. A player who voted for either tied Target satisfies the voting requirement and may survive, subject to the Ambush rules.
answers.evidence: Vote: tied players at the most votes are all Targets; each Target is eliminated unless protected by its own successful Ambush; with tied Targets, voting for any one of them satisfies the voting requirement.

answers.answer: No. Green is eliminated: Green did not vote for the Target (Blue), and the rule eliminates every other player who did not vote for any Target. Receiving no votes does not protect Green.
answers.evidence: Vote: “Every other player who did not vote for any Target is also eliminated,” subject to the successful Ambush exception.

answers.answer: Red's Ambush does not count as a vote; Yellow's vote for Red and Pink's vote for Yellow each count. Red and Yellow tie at one vote each, so both are Targets. Red's Ambush succeeds because Red is a Target. Yellow is eliminated by Red's legal retaliation; Red survives, and Pink survives because Pink voted for tied Target Yellow. Red and Pink remain for a Final Showdown.
answers.evidence: Three-player example: “Red plays Ambush, Yellow votes for Red, and Pink votes for Yellow. Red and Yellow tie at one vote each and are both Targets. Yellow is eliminated; Red survives ... Pink voted for tied Target Yellow and survives, leaving Red and Pink for a Final Showdown.”

answers.answer: No. A successful Ambusher chooses one player who voted for them to eliminate, even if four players voted for them. They cannot choose an arbitrary player or someone who voted for a different Target.
answers.evidence: Ambush: a successful Ambusher chooses “one of the players who voted for them” and “cannot choose an arbitrary player or someone who voted for a different Target.”

answers.answer: The Ambush fails, and that player eliminates themselves.
answers.evidence: Ambush: “An Ambush played by someone who is not a Target fails: that player eliminates themselves.”

answers.answer: No gold is awarded at four survivors. The round continues with another conspiracy and vote among the four survivors, using only surviving players in subsequent votes.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure: “Three or more” survivors “continue with another conspiracy and vote among survivors”; subsequent votes use only surviving players.

answers.answer: The sole survivor collects all four central Gold Bar cards. They are not four points: each card is worth 3, 4, or 5 points, and the card values may differ.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure: one survivor “collects all four central Gold Bars.” Components: Gold Bars are cards, each with a value of 3, 4, or 5 points.

answers.answer: The two survivors resolve a Final Showdown for the central Gold Bars. Each takes a set of Share, Steal, and Grab One & Go cards. They may discuss intentions and a bargain, then each chooses one card and places it face down; when both are ready, they reveal simultaneously and use the payoff table.
answers.evidence: Final Showdown: each takes a set containing Share, Steal, and Grab One & Go; they may discuss; each chooses one face down; when both are ready, reveal simultaneously.

answers.answer: Each player who was not participating in the final vote receives one Gold Bar from the deck. Players who participated in that final vote receive no consolation bar for this outcome, including those eliminated in it. Nobody collects the four central bars: leave them for the next round and add no new bars.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure, zero survivors: each player “not participating in the final vote” gets one bar from the deck; leave the four central bars for next round and add no new bars. Special Rules: final voters receive no consolation bar.

answers.answer: Each finalist receives two Gold Bar cards.
answers.evidence: Final Showdown table, Share versus Share: “You get 2; opponent gets 2.”

answers.answer: The finalist choosing Share receives zero bars; the finalist choosing Steal receives all four central bars.
answers.evidence: Final Showdown table, Share versus Steal: “You get 0; opponent gets 4.”

answers.answer: The finalist choosing Grab One & Go receives one bar, and the finalist choosing Steal receives the other three bars.
answers.evidence: Final Showdown table, Grab One & Go versus Steal: “You get 1; opponent gets 3.” The summary also says Grab One & Go always gives its player exactly one bar.

answers.answer: The finalist choosing Grab One & Go receives one bar, and the finalist choosing Share receives the other three bars.
answers.evidence: Final Showdown table, Grab One & Go versus Share: “You get 1; opponent gets 3.” The summary also says Grab One & Go always gives its player exactly one bar.

answers.answer: Each finalist takes one central bar. The other two bars remain in the center. If play continues, deal just two new bars for the next round.
answers.evidence: Final Showdown: if both choose Grab One & Go, each receives one and the other two bars remain central; add just two new bars for the next round.

answers.answer: Neither finalist receives gold. Every other player receives one Gold Bar from the deck. Leave all four central bars for the next round and add no new gold to the central pool.
answers.evidence: Final Showdown: on double Steal, “neither finalist receives gold”; give every other player one bar from the deck; leave all four central bars for next round and add no new gold.

answers.answer: Victory is checked at the end of a round, after Gold Bars have been awarded, regardless of how the round ended. With 6–9 players, the threshold is at least 25 points; with 10–12 players, it is at least 24 points. If multiple players qualify with different totals, the highest point total wins.
answers.evidence: Scoring / Victory Conditions: check “at the end of a round, after Gold Bars have been awarded”; thresholds are 25 points (6–9 players) and 24 points (10–12); “the highest point total wins.”

answers.answer: If exactly two qualifying players tie for the highest Gold point total, they conduct another Final Showdown. Repeat Showdowns as necessary until a single player anywhere at the table has the highest total. If a normal round ends without a winner, everyone returns for the next round: stand all Player ID cards upright.
answers.evidence: Scoring / Victory Conditions: tied highest qualifying totals conduct another Final Showdown; “Repeat these Showdowns as necessary until a single player anywhere at the table has the highest gold point total.” Turn Structure: if there is no winner, “everyone returns: stand all Player ID cards upright.”
